picks.d: THE weekend. Charli XCX, The Strokes, Rüfüs Du Sol headline. The xx, GloRilla, Death Cab for Cutie, PinkPantheress, Djo, Lucy Dacus, Ethel Cain, Modest Mouse. Three days of music, food, wine, and beer in Golden Gate Park.
One of the greatest voices alive, for free, in the eucalyptus amphitheater. Free tickets via lottery at sterngrove.org. Destani Wolf opens. Doors at noon.
The homestand is back! Friday 7:15pm, Saturday 4:15pm (Wall of Fame Ceremony), Sunday 1:05pm (Corduroy Hat giveaway). Waterfront baseball is back.
San Francisco's annual celebration of Filipino culture. Live performances, art, food vendors, and community. One of the city's most vibrant cultural festivals.

picks.t: Treasures of the Pharaohs · de Young
picks.d: Ancient Egyptian artifacts from the Valley of the Kings making their U.S. debut. 130 rare objects from the tomb of Yuya and Thuya. This will be packed all fall — go now.
Six home games in one week. Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday against Houston. Midweek baseball is underrated — smaller crowds, better seats, same garlic fries.
Nearly 200 pieces of ancient Italian art, gold jewelry, and ceramics from a civilization that thrived before Rome. The Legion of Honor is worth the trip just for the building.
East LA legends at the outdoor amphitheater in Saratoga. Bring a layer, grab wine before the show. If you're not at Outside Lands, this is your Friday night.
Peak viewing nights for the year's best meteor shower. Get out of the city — Mt. Tam, Pacifica, or anywhere with dark skies. Free, spectacular, and worth staying up for.
Circus-theater love letter to SF's weird history. Aerial acrobatics, shadow play, live music. Use code 49FOR49 for $49 tickets.

picks.t: Free Museum Day · Asian Art Museum
picks.d: Free admission to explore the permanent collection. Also check Conservatory of Flowers and de Young for free days this month.
Two-time Emmy and five-time Grammy nominee performing the Great American Songbook. One night only. Intimate and classy.

ongoing.d: Public Enemy (Sat Aug 15 — special Saturday show), Al Green (Aug 16). Final two shows of the season. All free.
130+ free lunchtime concerts near Market St through late September.
Monthly evening market with food vendors, DJs, and pop-ups along the waterfront.
Free community yoga Saturdays at 10am. Bring your own mat.
Free classic arcade games, cheap drinks, DJ nights on weekends. Divisadero.
Free readings, book launches, and poetry nights in North Beach almost every week.
Every Sunday 7am–3pm. SF's oldest flea market. Free to browse, cash only.

new.name: Bar Coto
new.d: From the A16 team. Espresso and pastries morning, sandwiches at lunch, low-ABV cocktails at night.

new.name: Esme
new.d: New French restaurant in the old Ragazza space. Pastas, roast chicken, lush back patio.

new.name: JouJou
new.d: From the Lazy Bear team. French-leaning, seafood-heavy. One of the most exciting openings of the year.

new.name: Dingles Public House
new.d: Fish and chips, sausage rolls, Sunday roast. British food done right on Fulton St.

classic.name: Jollibee
classic.d: Now open at 934 Market. Fried chicken, Jolly Spaghetti, Peach Mango Pie. Lines still long.

classic.name: Zuni Café
classic.d: Caesar salad, roast chicken for two, the marble bar. SF's forever restaurant.

classic.name: La Taqueria
classic.d: The taco that launched a thousand arguments. No rice, good beans, great carnitas.

classic.name: Tony's Pizza Napoletana
classic.d: 13-time world pizza champion. Try the Margherita or the Cal Italia. Worth the wait.

bars.name: Big Finish Wine
bars.d: 48 wines on tap, most under $14. Organized by finish. Nobody bothers you here.

bars.name: Bar Shoji
bars.d: Coffee by day, cocktail den at night. Wagyu-fat-washed whisky.

bars.name: The DeLuxe
bars.d: Legendary jazz bar. Live music nightly, $5–15 cover.

bars.name: Valley Club
bars.d: Hotel G mezzanine. Low lights, velvet, cocoa-butter Negroni.

bars.name: The Green Heron
bars.d: Classic cocktails, Miller Lite, no judgment.

bars.name: Jilli
bars.d: Makgeolli from teapots, popcorn fried chicken. Communal and loud.

bars.name: Standard Deviant
bars.d: Waterfront taproom at Pier 70. Barrel-aged rosé-saison.

bars.name: Rikki's
bars.d: Women-focused bar. Watch parties, lavender cocktails, wings.

sports.note: Six home games this week! Best homestand of the month.

games.teams: Saturday: The Strokes, The xx, Djo
Sunday: Rüfüs Du Sol, Death Cab

sports.note: 3-day passes sold out. Single-day still available.
Indie baseball at Raimondi Park. oaklandballers.com for schedule.

concerts.d: Charli XCX, The Strokes, Rüfüs Du Sol headline. 60+ acts across Golden Gate Park.
Free at Stern Grove. One of the greatest voices alive. Reserve at sterngrove.org.
East LA legends at the outdoor amphitheater. The non-Outside Lands Friday option.
Great American Songbook. Two-time Emmy nominee. One night only.
Circus-theater in North Beach. Code 49FOR49 for $49 tickets.
Broadway musical all summer. Intimate theater, every seat is good.

concertsOngoing.d: Public Enemy (Sat Aug 15), Al Green (Aug 16). Last two shows of the season. All free.
Haight St jazz bar. Jazz, soul, funk nightly. $5–15 cover.
Aug 14 & 16. Time travel back to the 70s at the Filoli estate in Woodside.

singles.d: 60,000 people in one park. Easiest place to talk to strangers all year. Go alone, meet everyone.
Cultural festival with amazing food, performances, and community energy. Great solo activity.
Join astronomy meetup groups heading to dark sky spots. Shared blankets, shared wonder.
Classic speed dating at a brewery. 5-minute rounds, real faces.
Kickball, soccer, volleyball, pickleball — join solo, get placed on a team.

singlesOngoing.d: November Project (free, Wed+Fri 6:30am). Midnight Runners (Thu nights).
Salsa and bachata lessons + open dancing. No partner needed.
Green Apple Books and City Lights host regular reading groups.
Pottery at Claymakers, cooking at 18 Reasons, dance at ODC.

date.title: Stern Grove & Sunset
date.tagline: Patti LaBelle for free, then sunset at Ocean Beach.

steps.title: Arrive at Stern Grove
steps.detail: Get there early for a good spot. Bring a blanket, snacks, and layers. Doors at noon, show at 2.

steps.title: Patti LaBelle live
steps.detail: One of the greatest voices in music, surrounded by eucalyptus trees. This is a core SF memory.

steps.title: Walk to Ocean Beach
steps.detail: 15-minute drive or 30-minute bus. Watch the sunset, grab tacos at Outerlands or burritos at Underdogs.

date.title: Baseball & Cocktails
date.tagline: Giants game, garlic fries, waterfront drinks.

steps.title: Pre-game at Anchor Brewing taproom
steps.detail: Grab a beer before the game. Short walk to Oracle Park.

steps.title: Giants vs. Tigers
steps.detail: Friday night baseball at Oracle Park. Garlic fries, crab sandwich, and the bay behind the outfield.

steps.title: Nightcap at Bar Shoji
steps.detail: The coffee shop has transformed into a cocktail den. Wagyu-fat-washed whisky in a moody room.

date.title: Outside Lands Date
date.tagline: Music festival by day, nice dinner by night.

steps.title: Outside Lands — afternoon set
steps.detail: Pick a day pass. Saturday has The Strokes and The xx. Wander between stages, eat at the food stalls.

steps.title: Slip out for dinner
steps.detail: Leave before the headliner. Cab to JouJou in the Mission — new French-California from the Lazy Bear team.

steps.title: Back for the headliner
steps.detail: Return for The Strokes or whoever's closing. The park at night is magic.

solo.title: Park, Music & Stars
solo.tagline: Golden Gate Park, free music, meteor shower.

steps.title: Coffee and the park
steps.detail: Walk through Golden Gate Park. Japanese Tea Garden, bison paddock, botanical garden.

steps.title: Patti LaBelle at Stern Grove
steps.detail: Free concert. Bring a blanket, close your eyes. Nobody knows you're here.

steps.title: Perseids Meteor Shower
steps.detail: Drive to Mt. Tam or Pacifica. Bring a blanket. The sky puts on a show.

solo.title: Museum, Wine & Jazz
solo.tagline: A day that feels like a vacation.

steps.title: Treasures of the Pharaohs
steps.detail: De Young museum. Ancient Egyptian artifacts. Go at your own pace.

steps.title: Lunch in the park
steps.detail: De Young cafe or walk to Nopalito on 9th Ave.

steps.title: Wine at Big Finish
steps.detail: 48 wines on tap. Grab a seat at the bar, try a few glasses.

steps.title: Jazz at The DeLuxe
steps.detail: Live music on Haight. $5–10 cover. Perfect solo evening.

steps.title: Outside Lands
steps.detail: Solo festival days are underrated. You go where you want, see who you want, eat what you want.

steps.title: Find the food stalls
steps.detail: Outside Lands has some of SF's best restaurants doing festival menus. Eat your way through.

steps.title: Close out with the headliner
steps.detail: Dance alone in the crowd. Nobody cares. Everyone's having the same experience.

birthday.title: Festival & Group Dinner
birthday.tagline: No planning required. Just show up.

steps.title: Stern Grove — Patti LaBelle
steps.detail: Meet everyone at the amphitheater. Free, outdoors, legendary performer. Easy birthday activity.

steps.title: Dolores Park
steps.detail: Grab Bi-Rite ice cream. Sunset on the hill. Bring a speaker.

steps.title: Dinner at Jilli
steps.detail: Korean communal food. Makgeolli, fried chicken. Tell them it's your birthday.

birthday.title: Giants Game Birthday
birthday.tagline: Garlic fries and a scoreboard birthday message.

steps.title: Pre-game drinks
steps.detail: Meet the crew at the Yard at Mission Rock, right next to the ballpark.

steps.title: Giants vs. Tigers
steps.detail: Friday night baseball. You can get a birthday message on the scoreboard if you call ahead.

steps.title: Bars in the Mission
steps.detail: Big Finish for wine, then Green Heron for shots. Birthday person drinks free (morally, not legally).

birthday.title: Outside Lands Birthday
birthday.tagline: Three days. Your whole crew. Golden Gate Park.

steps.title: Outside Lands — full day
steps.detail: Get 3-day passes for the group. This IS the birthday party.

steps.title: Group dinner break
steps.detail: Sneak out to Esme in NoPa. New French spot with a back patio. Toast properly.

steps.title: Back for the headliner
steps.detail: Charli XCX on Friday, The Strokes on Saturday, Rüfüs on Sunday. Pick your night.

steps.title: Coffee at Equator in the Presidio
steps.detail: Good coffee, incredible setting. Walk toward the bridge from here.

steps.title: Walk the Golden Gate Bridge
steps.detail: Halfway and back. Your friends will take 400 photos.

steps.title: Lunch in Japantown
steps.detail: If Pistahan is happening this weekend, even better. Otherwise, Marufuku for ramen.

steps.title: Patti LaBelle at Stern Grove
steps.detail: Free concert. Bring a blanket. Your friends won't believe this is free.

friends.title: Mission Day → Giants Night
friends.tagline: Neighborhoods by day, baseball by night.

steps.title: Dolores Park
steps.detail: Bi-Rite ice cream, blanket, skyline view. Peak SF.

steps.title: Walk Valencia Street
steps.detail: Paxton Gate, Sightglass coffee, bookstores.

steps.title: Giants vs. Tigers
steps.detail: Friday night Oracle Park. Waterfront baseball, garlic fries.

friends.title: Outside Lands Weekend
friends.tagline: The big one. Plan nothing else.

steps.title: Outside Lands
steps.detail: Get the 3-day pass. This is the weekend.

steps.title: Dinner at JouJou
steps.detail: New French-California from the Lazy Bear team. The buzzy opening.

steps.title: Back for headliners
steps.detail: The Strokes, Charli XCX, Rüfüs Du Sol. Every night is different.

steps.title: Ferry Building farmers market
steps.detail: Saturday morning market. Pastries, olive oils, waterfront walk. Parents love this.

steps.title: Lunch on the water
steps.detail: Hog Island oysters or takeaway on the benches with Bay Bridge views.

steps.title: Twin Peaks
steps.detail: 360° view of the city. Your mom will say 'wow' at least four times.

steps.title: Coffee in Noe Valley
steps.detail: 24th Street. Quiet, charming, easy walking.

parents.title: Museums & Nice Dinner
parents.tagline: Art, history, and somewhere impressive for dinner.

steps.title: Treasures of the Pharaohs
steps.detail: Ancient Egyptian artifacts just opened at the de Young. Impressive and easy to navigate.

steps.title: Lunch in Hayes Valley
steps.detail: Absinthe for French brasserie, or walk Hayes Street.

steps.title: Japanese Tea Garden
steps.detail: Golden Gate Park. Peaceful, beautiful. Green tea and cookies.

steps.title: Dinner at Esme
steps.detail: New French restaurant in NoPa. The kind of place your parents will tell their friends about.

steps.title: The Etruscans at Legion of Honor
steps.detail: Nearly 200 pieces of ancient Italian art and gold jewelry. The building alone is worth the trip.

steps.title: Lunch at Cliff House area
steps.detail: Views of the Pacific. Easy drive from Legion of Honor.

steps.title: Dinner at Zuni Café
steps.detail: Roast chicken for two, Caesar salad, a bottle of wine. Your parents will love this.
